scenarios.title: Guessed VPN password, then hidden PowerShell download
scenarios.story: maria's password was guessed from 203.0.113.77; minutes later her workstation ran hidden, encoded PowerShell that pulled a script from the IOC server and ran discovery commands.

scenarios.title: Three mistyped passwords at the user's own desk
scenarios.story: tom mistyped his password three times on his own workstation at his usual time and IP, then read mail and opened Teams as on every other day.

scenarios.title: Nightly software-deployment PowerShell
scenarios.story: The deployment agent (ccmexec.exe) runs the same encoded update script as svc_deploy every night at 02:00 and reaches only the internal package share.

scenarios.title: Password spray against eight accounts, no success
scenarios.story: 198.51.100.66 tried one password against eight accounts within three minutes. No attempt succeeded: an attack, but no compromise.

scenarios.title: One connection to a listed IOC, no endpoint telemetry
scenarios.story: A lab machine connected once to a listed IOC. There are no process or logon events for it, so what made the connection cannot be known from this data.

scenarios.title: Wazuh: SSH brute force, login, then a UID 0 user created
scenarios.story: 192.0.2.150 guessed deploy's SSH password on web-02 and created a root-level account 'sysupd' four minutes later (Wazuh alerts).

scenarios.title: Failures then success from an unfamiliar external IP, nothing after
scenarios.story: lena usually connects from 198.51.100.20; this evening she failed four times from 192.0.2.44 and then got in. Travel and a new home router fit as well as a stolen password; nothing after the login tells them apart.

scenarios.title: Word macro starts hidden PowerShell, IOC download, scheduled task
scenarios.story: priya opened Invoice_4471.docm; Word started hidden, encoded PowerShell that downloaded from the listed IOC address 192.0.2.77 and created a logon task.

scenarios.title: Domain logon script runs PowerShell hidden every morning
scenarios.story: Group Policy (gpscript.exe) runs the NETLOGON drive-mapping script with a hidden window at every logon on kim's workstation; it reaches only the file server.

scenarios.title: Six users mistype once each through the usual Citrix gateway
scenarios.story: Six staff who log on through CTX-GW01 (10.30.0.5) every morning each failed once and succeeded 25 seconds later. By source it looks like a spray, but each account got in on its second try from its usual source.

scenarios.title: Wazuh (Windows): RDP guessing, logon, shadow copies deleted
scenarios.story: 198.51.100.200 guessed Administrator's password over RDP on WIN-FS01 and deleted all volume shadow copies seven minutes later, a ransomware precursor.

scenarios.title: Developer pipes a web installer into Invoke-Expression
scenarios.story: omar ran 'iex (irm https://tools.example.net/install.ps1)' from Windows Terminal. Many developer tools install this way, and so does malware; the script's content and what it did afterwards are not in the data.

scenarios.title: Backup service account guessed over VPN from a listed spray source
scenarios.story: svc_backup only ever logs on from the backup server; at 03:12 it was guessed over VPN from 192.0.2.77, an address on the IOC list as a password-spray source.
